title: The wheel turned
hookLine: the first sermon and the five companions (Buddhacarita 15)

cards: Five men in a park near Benares see someone walking toward them, and they make a plan. They know him. They practiced hard beside him once, fasting and straining, until he gave it up and started eating again.
They decided he'd gone soft. So as he comes closer, they agree: we won't stand up for him. We won't greet him.
Let him sit where he likes. Then he arrives, and the plan doesn't survive the moment.

teach.b: First, the welcome they didn't intend. In the poem, as he draws near, the five find themselves rising anyway. The Vinaya's telling adds the details: one takes his bowl and robe, one brings water, one makes ready a seat.
Their agreement falls apart in their hands. They still speak to him as an old friend, by name, and he tells them gently not to: he has become something new. Second, the middle way.
What he teaches first is not a list of rules.
It's a road between two ditches. On one side, the life of pleasure he left in the palace. On the other, the self-punishment these five still believe in, the starving and the straining.
Neither leads to peace, he says.
There is a middle path, and it is the one he found. Third, the truths. He names suffering, its arising, its ending, and the path that leads to its ending.
And he lays out that path: right view, right resolve, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
The poem sets all of this into verse, so the first teaching becomes something you could almost sing.
Fourth, the first one who sees. Kaundinya, one of the five, understands.
The discourses say that when he did, a cry went up through the heavens: the wheel of the teaching has been set rolling, and no one in the world can turn it back. A wheel, once pushed, keeps rolling.
The Buddha gave it the first push, in a deer park, to five men who had planned not to stand up.

how: The first teaching is remembered in Buddhist communities; in Theravada lands the full moon of Asalha (Asalha Puja) marks it, and the wheel, the dharma-chakra, appears on temple roofs, gates and flags as a sign of the teaching.

o: a wheel of fortune that rises and falls
the wheel of the teaching, set rolling
a chariot wheel from his palace days

games.q: the first teaching: tap the pairs.
p: the first of the five to understand
set rolling, and no one can turn it back

s: the five companions ran to greet him the moment they saw him
they agreed not to stand up for him, and then found themselves rising anyway.
the first teaching says harsh self-punishment is the way to peace
it names self-torment as one of the two ditches, beside a life of pleasure.
Kaundinya was the first of the five to understand
and the discourses say a cry went up that the wheel had been set rolling.

games.q: you're one of the five. the man you think gave up is walking toward you. you've all agreed not to stand. what happens?
o: you walk away before he arrives.
games.why: the agreement falls apart as he comes near: they rise, and the Vinaya says they took his bowl, brought water and made ready a seat.

practice: Think of one place where you swing between two ditches, all in or all out, work all night or not at all, and try to say the middle of it in one plain line, the way you'd tell a friend.
Not a rule, just a road between the two; then let the line go and rest with the breath.

wordCard.voice: Dharmacakra, the wheel of the teaching, turned for the first time: the middle way, the truths and the path, taught to five old companions in a deer park, and Kaundinya understands. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit dharmacakra, the wheel of the teaching (Pali dhammacakka).

carryVoice: Your line: the wheel, in verse. Once it was pushed, no one could turn it back. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Buddhacarita 15 (the journey to Benares, the five, the first teaching)
Vinaya, Mahavagga 1.6 (the five rise despite their agreement: bowl, water, seat)
